changed.title: Small cases only: some n by n graph, n >= 3, has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of s gates on the one-a-side promise and no AND/OR one of at most s + 2n - 5 gates
changed.statement: ¬ (∀ (n s : ℕ) (A : Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), 3 ≤ n → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → C.size ≤ s → PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C → PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost A (s + (2 * n - 5)))
changed.unlocks: settles this statement on the record; whichever side is proved is kept
changed.context: Truth unknown; our support is small cases only. An answer is one graph with n at least 3 and two circuits in one file: an AND/OR/NOT circuit of s gates right on the promise, and a proof that no AND/OR circuit of at most s + 2n - 5 gates is. The first place to look is side 3, where the bound is s + 1: a 3 by 3 graph that costs 6 with NOT gates and 8 or more without would answer it. We know of none. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.

changed.title: Fixing a degree-two vertex v of a graph with no 4-cycle, where G - v and G - N[v] keep an edge, saves at least three gates at false or at least four at true
changed.statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : List (Fin n × Fin n)) (v u w : Fin n) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), (∀ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ e.2) → (∀ a b c d : Fin n, a ≠ c → b ≠ d → ((a, b) ∈ E ∨ (b, a) ∈ E) → ((b, c) ∈ E ∨ (c, b) ∈ E) → ((c, d) ∈ E ∨ (d, c) ∈ E) → ((d, a) ∈ E ∨ (a, d) ∈ E) → False) → u ≠ w → ((v, u) ∈ E ∨ (u, v) ∈ E) → ((v, w) ∈ E ∨ (w, v) ∈ E) → (∀ z : Fin n, ((v, z) ∈ E ∨ (z, v) ∈ E) → z = u ∨ z = w) → (∃ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ v ∧ e.2 ≠ v) → (∃ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ v ∧ e.2 ≠ v ∧ e.1 ≠ u ∧ e.2 ≠ u ∧ e.1 ≠ w ∧ e.2 ≠ w) → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => x e.1 && x e.2)) → (∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo D ∧ D.size + 3 ≤ C.size ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, D.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => Function.update x v false e.1 && Function.update x v false e.2)) ∨ (∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo D ∧ D.size + 4 ≤ C.size ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, D.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => Function.update x v true e.1 && Function.update x v true e.2))

changed.context: Truth unknown to us. By exact values it holds at 312 of the 313 degree-two vertices of the checked small graphs; the one failure is the 3-path at its middle, which 'some edge avoids v' excludes (computed). Cut by the gates listing x_v in a least C: three or more readers, two readers with an AND or NOT, two OR readers, or a constant climbing two levels close by constant propagation; a lone AND reader read by an OR closes by pruning, 3 at false. OPEN: x_v's lone reader is an OR that an AND lists: the cuts give 1 at false and 3 at true. A proof there must rebuild, not only cut.

changed.title: Majority of 7 bits (at least 4 on): at most 21 AND, OR, NOT gates, none dead, a NOT on a gate
changed.statement: ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack 7 C ∧ C.size ≤ 21 ∧ (∀ x : Fin 7 → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = decide (4 ≤ (List.ofFn x).count true)) ∧ (∀ j < C.size, C.output = 7 + j ∨ ∃ i < C.size, j < i ∧ 7 + j ∈ (C.gates.getD i ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, []⟩).inputs) ∧ (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not → 7 ≤ g.inputs.headD 0 → (C.gates.getD (g.inputs.headD 0 - 7) ⟨PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and, []⟩).op ≠ PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not) ∧ (∃ g ∈ C.gates, g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not ∧ 7 ≤ g.inputs.headD 0)
changed.unlocks: whether a NOT gate can be at work at the best known size for this function
changed.context: Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND, OR or NOT, at most two earlier wires each; wires 0 to 6 the inputs, gate j writes wire 7+j) and the output wire, judged on every input. 21 is the size of the best AND/OR circuit the checker has accepted, so a yes is a circuit with a NOT at work that ties it. A circuit where the NOT and the gate reading it can be deleted and the rest is still right satisfies this row and shows nothing; say whether yours survives that deletion. So does a NOT-free circuit three gates smaller with one gate rewritten through NOTs; say if yours is one.
changed.sketch: A circuit three gates below our NOT-free bar also answers this; a calibration of our constructions, no claim attached either way. Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND, OR or NOT, at most two earlier wires each; wires 0 to 6 the inputs, gate j writes wire 7+j) and the output wire, judged on every input. 21 is the size of the best AND/OR circuit the checker has accepted. A NOT-free circuit of 18 gates with its last gate rewritten through NOTs meets every clause, and so does a circuit whose NOT can be deleted; say which kind yours is.
